plan.title: Colon RSEM DE: 6 treated vs 6 control + Hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The data profile gives 12000 genes x 12 samples of RSEM gene-level expected counts (non-integer) for 6 treated vs 6 control colon samples, single batch, unpaired, with sample_01 flagged at ~4x below median library size. Because the per-sample genes.results files carrying effective lengths were not delivered, the tximport(type='rsem')+length-offset path that the knowledge service names as the correct RSEM import cannot be run — there is no gene-level effective-length matrix in this environment to build it from (confirmed: no such reference is staged, and tximport itself is not an installed package). The plan therefore proceeds on the delivered gene x sample count matrix alone: round the non-integer RSEM expected counts to nearest integer (necessary for DESeq2's negative-binomial machinery) and run the standard DESeq2 workflow without a length offset, explicitly documenting this deviation and its consequence (uncorrected inter-gene length bias in absolute levels; the treated-vs-control comparison per gene is largely unaffected since length is constant within a gene across samples, but cross-gene comparisons and any length-driven pathway bias are not corrected). Track 1 runs sample-structure QC (keeping and reporting the low-depth sample per the flagged rule rather than silently dropping it), minimal pre-filtering, DESeq2 Wald test with an explicit reference level (control) and apeglm shrinkage, BH-adjusted results at alpha 0.05, and a secondary edgeR quasi-likelihood run for a robustness overlap check (both packages confirmed installed). Track 2 takes the DESeq2 Wald statistic ranked list into fgsea preranked GSEA against the MSigDB Hallmark gene sets (confirmed staged for human), with WikiPathways and Reactome as staged follow-up collections. A final report step assembles the DE table, QC/fit diagnostics, the two-method overlap, and the enrichment results with all methodological caveats stated.
